about: Labels for requests.json, written by reading the notes; one entry per request.

cases.why: The marriage proof list and the spouse packet (forms, sealed medical with the firm's doctor) say what to gather.
Ben's fee sheet has the N-400 fee, and the firm files N-400s online, so the online fee applies.
Lucia is in Thursdays 9 to 2 and needs 48 hours notice by text for other times.
Puentes has a fixed shape, and the only free consult day is the citizenship clinic on the second Saturday of November.
Asylum is a $5,500 flat fee and can go on a plan; near the one-year deadline it is filed whatever the balance.
Cooking question, nothing to do with the firm.
No note covers missed biometrics appointments or rescheduling them.
H-1B work is only for three repeat employers who pay all fees; a new employer goes to Teresa; intake starts with a conflict check.
A first consult is $150 paid at booking and credited if they hire the firm; free screenings only at the clinic.
The firm's everyday words for green card, work permit and travel permit keep it plain and easy to translate.
No refund rule is written down, but unearned advance fees stay in trust until earned at the engagement letter milestones.
Ben calendars the one-year date at intake and anyone ten months past arrival is flagged to Teresa the same day.
The prep session note has the bring list and the mock interview two weeks before.
Unit conversion, nothing to do with the firm.
Client deposits go into the IOLTA trust account and never mix with operating money.
The firm's marriage proof list (lease, joint accounts, insurance, tax return, photos, affidavits) gives the other evidence to use.
Lucia is a $45 an hour contractor who invoices monthly; her invoices are never paid from trust.
RFE timelines, the two-week interview prep session and the newsletter dates set the plan; asylum near the deadline goes first.
Defensive cases are taken only if the person is not detained; detained removal and criminal matters are referred out.
Plan terms: payments due on the 1st, $25 late fee, and two missed payments pause the work until Teresa talks with the client.
General coding question, nothing to do with the firm.
No parent note exists; the spouse packet is the firm's closest bundle (minus the I-130A), with the sponsor income rule.
A logistical reminder; useful are the text channel, the 24 hour rescheduling rule and no emojis or exclamation marks.
An RFE response is a $600 flat fee, free if the firm caused it; hourly work is rare.
Ben runs the conflict check in DocketLeaf on every name involved before booking.
Call advance parole a travel permit; the firm usually files the I-131 with the green card packet.
Sports trivia, nothing to do with the firm.
No note sets a response time promise for calls or emails.
Each issue has one explainer on what clients asked most; clinic, portal and case types give non-asylum topics.
Ben fills in forms and checks fees while legal judgment stays with Teresa; no note names fee waivers directly.
Ben scans every USCIS notice into DocketLeaf the day it arrives; the portal and plain words cover telling the client.
No file retention rule; the six years in the trust note is for reconciliation reports only.
When turning someone away the firm gives two referral names and the state bar referral line, never just a no.
Personal school project question, nothing to do with the firm.
Lucia bills one rate, $45 an hour, as a contractor; no separate court rate is noted.
Fee $5,500 before government fees, next step is three declaration sessions with Lucia, and updates go through the portal.
Arithmetic question, nothing to do with the firm.
RFEs usually allow 87 days; Ben first scans it and calendars the printed due date, target mailing by day 60.
